standard.title: Develop narratives and observations
standard.description: develop narratives and share observations, using sources, and subject-specific terms
standard.prior_knowledge: From Foundation (AC9HSFS05): Students shared narratives using sources and basic time/place terms.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students develop narratives and share observations about the past and places, using sources and subject-specific terms for time sequence.

nodes.label: Time sequence vocabulary
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use time sequence terms (then, now, yesterday, today, past, present, later on, before I was born, in the future, generations) correctly in spoken and written communication.
nodes.minimum_width: Use at least four time sequence terms accurately in a spoken or written description of a change over time.
nodes.typical_width: Use a full range of time sequence terms in speech and writing when describing family life over time and changes to places; use terms to order events and connect past to present.
wider: Explore how time sequence terms translate across languages represented in the class and discuss how different cultures describe the passage of time
Create a glossary of time sequence terms with student-generated definitions and examples
nodes.hinge_reason: Developing a historical narrative requires the vocabulary of time sequence — without these terms, students cannot express the relationship between past and present that HASS Year 1 demands.

response_modes.reason: Time sequence vocabulary requires deliberate, frequent practice across multiple contexts — use routines (morning meeting time talk, sequencing activities) to build fluency before expecting narrative use.

success_criteria: Uses at least four time sequence terms correctly in context
Terms are used to express temporal relationships, not randomly inserted

nodes.label: Retelling historical narratives
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can retell stories about life in the past through spoken narratives using pictures, role-plays or photographs, drawing on sources and using time sequence vocabulary.
nodes.minimum_width: Retell at least one story about life in the past using a source (photograph, drawing, role-play prop) and at least two time sequence terms.
nodes.typical_width: Retell stories about life in the past through spoken narratives and the use of pictures, role-plays or photographs; use time sequence terms naturally; draw on collected information from oral histories, objects and photographs.
wider: Develop an extended narrative that traces change from past to present using multiple sources
Create a multimodal narrative (images + text + speech) about how a local place or aspect of family life has changed

response_modes.reason: Historical narrative integrates collected information, time vocabulary and personal/family perspective into a communicative whole — the narrative is the Year 1 HASS communicating endpoint.

success_criteria: Retells a narrative about life in the past using at least one source
Uses at least two time sequence terms accurately within the narrative
